video.title: 14 BORING Businesses That Need No Storefront (And Still Pay Like One)

summary: A narrated listicle (with a fictional character 'Harry') combining seven spare-room businesses (Etsy resale, candles/soap, labels, cup pressing, 3D printing, laser engraving, shared-mail postcards) with seven land leases (grazing, hunting, timber, event parking, truck parking, solar, gravel royalties). It gives typical revenue ranges, startup costs and a few named examples. Key takeaways: price machine time and waste, chase repeat local buyers, and write leases with renewal dates and escalators. The shared postcard is presented as the best spare-room option and gravel royalties as the biggest land ceiling.

lessons.lesson: One-off sales are the sample; repeat local business buyers are the income.

quote.text: Oneoff sales are your sample. A local business that reorders is your income
quote.speaker: Narrator

lessons.lesson: Saved rent is the margin: a home business keeps what a shop pays its landlord.
Low entry costs or modest equipment hurdles act as moats because serious people ignore them.
Shrink the market: you need 40 buyers out of thousands, or 3-4 local accounts, not millions.
Zero-build leases: others bring equipment, you bring land and a signature.
Permits and bonds that are hard to get are the strongest moats.

quote.text: Hard to get means hard to copy
quote.speaker: Narrator

lessons.lesson: Every lease needs a renewal date and an escalator.
Shared costs are the product: sell the spread between solo and shared mailing cost.

evidence_quality.rationale: Second-hand listicle with ranges and some cited examples; composite fictional character; likely scripted/AI-narrated; US-specific data.

extraction.review_notes: The extraction is thorough: all 14 ideas are captured, and the numbers, currencies and garbled figures (the $161/ton and $150 to $2.50 mis-speaks) are handled sensibly. The main fixes are three items understated as 'mention' depth and the postcard wrongly flagged as the primary idea in a two-part listicle. Several cited metric claims were missed (Rachel Smith/Dalton Joiner, Nick Fortosis, the gravel royalty range, the event-parking average and Harry's fictional result). Evidence rating C is appropriate.
